query:
Ugh, I swear the community garden’s tomato plants are out to get me this year. I stopped by to water them first thing this morning, tripped over a stray cucumber vine that’d snaked all the way across the path, and landed right in a patch of leaf lettuce that I’ve been babying for three weeks. My favorite canvas tote got covered in damp clover and mud, and a sparrow that was perched on the fence stole half the blueberry scone I’d stuffed in my pocket for a post-watering snack before I could even get up. I had to detour home to change out of my dirt-streaked jeans before heading to the store, which made me run way later than I planned.
Hey, I’m browsing the pantry staples section right now and need something with really simple, no-fuss ingredients, y’know? I’m looking for a decent price that feels fair for what I’m getting, nothing that feels like a total ripoff. Oh, and make sure whatever you pull up is certified non-GMO, I don’t want anything weird in there even if that’s not the main thing I’m focused on. I just need the standard multi-pack size they usually sell, not some random tiny travel size or giant bulk thing that’ll take me forever to get through.
